processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Controlling the cooling rate (air-assisted spraying for fast cooling, or air/furnace cooling for slow cooling) allows prediction of austenite structure decomposition and κ precipitation for improvement of mechanical properties.

precipitates.distribution: within austenite grains and along the grain boundary

structures.overall_structure: Slow cooling of Fe–28Mn–8.5Al–1C–1.2Si austenite below about -4.4 °C/h causes γ decomposition with κ-carbide precipitation; the slow-cooling fields in the TTT diagram include γ+κ*, γ+κ*+α(E2/DO3), γ+κ+B2/DO3, and γ+κ+κ*+α(B2/DO3).

unmapped_findings: The κ phase decomposes from the austenite matrix of Fe–28Mn–8.5Al–1C–1.2Si low-density steel when the cooling rate is slower than -4.4 °C h⁻¹ (Figure 3; caption in b0048 typographically writes the last alloying element as 1.2S).

For this high-Al (≥7 wt% Al) Fe–28Mn–8.5Al–1C–1.2Si steel, κ precipitation (rather than Fe(Mn)C carbide, which occurs in low-Al <7 wt% steels) forms within austenite grains and along grain boundaries.

Figure 3 slow-cooling reaction fields for Fe–28Mn–8.5Al–1C–1.2Si include: γ+κ* (field 3), γ+κ*+α(E2/DO3) (field 4), γ+κ+B2/DO3 (field 5), and γ+κ+κ*+α(B2/DO3); fast-cooling fields are γ (field 1) and γ+κ' (field 2).
